description: Issue #855 defect 2: an entry with red_tests=[] gives evaluate_red() nothing to iterate -- it can produce neither a `survived` nor an `unexpected` result, and used to fall straight through the (now-removed) old code path to a bare KILLED, without ever running a single assertion. That meant a comment-only/no-op mutant patch (this fixture's patch: adds one comment line, changes no behaviour) registered with red_tests=[] could pass the gate while proving nothing about any test's effectiveness. Before the fix: run_mutant.py --mutant _selftest-empty-red-tests-invalid --expect-verdict INVALID_MUTANT_EMPTY_RED_TESTS actually applied this no-op patch, built successfully (nothing changed), ran the (empty) red filter set, and reported KILLED -- proving the old code's blind spot for real, not just in theory. After the fix, validate_red_tests_declared() rejects the empty red_tests list before the patch is even applied.
target_symbol: N/A -- the patch is a no-op (comment-only); this fixture exists to prove an empty red_tests list is rejected, not to mutate real behaviour
